### T-451 · search: entries that hold only some of the words are listed after the full matches
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-451
- priority: P1 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-434
- why: `0 matches` tells an LLM that nothing is recorded, when one of its words was merely too many.
- summary: After the entries that hold every word, search lists the best entries that hold some of the words.
- depends: T-450, T-442
- files: src/cmd/search.rs, tests/cmd_search.rs, src/cmd/schema.rs
- read: docs/design.md, src/select.rs
- steps:
  1. src/cmd/search.rs: add `const PARTIAL_LIMIT: usize = 10;`. After the full matches are found, and only when more than one word was typed: take the items of all places that pass the filter and are not full matches, and rank them with `select::ranked(&rest, &Query { tags: Vec::new(), words })`, where `words` are the typed words and their glossary spellings. Keep the first PARTIAL_LIMIT. The line of such a result is its title.
  2. Text output: the full matches as before. When there are results with some of the words: the line `some of the words:`, then their lines in ranked order, and the last line is `<n> matches, <m> with some of the words` (with `1 match` when n is 1). Without such results the last line stays as it is today. With --full only the full matches are printed whole.
  3. JSON: every result gets `"match": "all"` or `"match": "some"`; the results with some of the words follow the full matches.
  4. src/cmd/schema.rs: only if it describes the fields of a search result, add `match` there; otherwise leave the file unchanged.
  5. tests/cmd_search.rs: add (a) `search valve rotor` with one entry holding both words and one holding only `rotor` in its title: the first is a match, the second comes after `some of the words:`, the last line is `1 match, 1 with some of the words`; (b) `search rotor nozzle` with no entry holding both prints `some of the words:` and `0 matches, 1 with some of the words`; (c) one typed word never prints `some of the words:`; (d) --json marks the results with `all` and `some`; (e) a draft is listed among them only with --drafts.
  6. Update the module comment. Run cargo test --test cmd_search and cargo test --test cmd_schema.
- accept: search lists up to 10 ranked entries that hold only some of the typed words, marked as such in text and JSON.
- verify: cargo test --test cmd_search && cargo test --test cmd_schema
- verified: 2026-11-25
- commit: 20d007b
- reqs: R-READ-3, R-READ-4
- by: Reynan Henry Tandoyo
- note (2026-11-25, planner): added
- note (2026-11-25, haiku-T-451): done

### T-454 · create.rs: unknown topics are refused, and an LLM's entry must name a topic
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-454
- priority: P1 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-435
- why: An LLM tags an entry only when the tool asks for it; this is the one place every new entry passes.
- summary: Once a project has topics, an entry cannot name a topic that is not on the list, and an LLM cannot write an entry without one.
- depends: T-452
- files: src/create.rs
- read: docs/design.md, docs/requirements.md
- steps:
  1. In `create::create`, before anything is queued: let `topics` be `tx.ctx().cfg.topics`. When it is empty, nothing is checked.
  2. Rule 1 (everyone): split the value of the field `topic` of `new.fields` at commas and trim each value. A value that equals no topic of the list ignoring case fails with Code::Usage and the message `unknown topic <value>; the topics of this project: <a, b, c> (dossier topics)`.
  3. Rule 2 (LLMs): when the writer is an LLM (`who.is_llm`), `tx.ctx().from_document` is None, the kind is Decision, Assumption, Finding, Lesson, Howto or Investigation, and the entry has no topic value, fail with Code::Refused and the message `an entry written by an LLM names its topic: --topic <one of a, b, c>`.
  4. Unit tests in src/create.rs, built as the existing tests of this file build their Tx: with topics [pumps, rig]: an LLM's finding without topic is refused; with `topic` = `Pumps` it is written; with `topic` = `valves` it is a usage error that names both topics; a person's finding without topic is written; an LLM's tool entry without topic is written; an LLM's finding from a document is written. With no topics in the settings, an LLM's finding without topic is written.
  5. Update the doc comment of `create` (the sentence `Refusing unknown tag values is not part of v0.1` gets the two rules added after it). Run cargo test --lib create::
- accept: create::create refuses an unknown topic for everyone and a missing topic for an LLM, only when the project has topics.
- verify: cargo test --lib create::
- verified: 2026-11-25
- commit: 55c9721
- reqs: R-TOPIC-2, R-TOPIC-3
- by: Reynan Henry Tandoyo
- note (2026-11-25, planner): added
- note (2026-11-25, haiku-T-454): done

### T-468 · codeptr.rs: what a code pointer covers
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-468
- priority: P1 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-436
- why: which and brief --task each had their own rule for when a pointer matches a path, and they differed.
- summary: One place decides whether an entry's pointer to code covers a given file.
- depends: T-440
- files: src/codeptr.rs, src/lib.rs
- read: docs/design.md, docs/format.md
- steps:
  1. src/lib.rs: add `pub mod codeptr;` in alphabetical order.
  2. src/codeptr.rs: `pub fn path_of(pointer: &str) -> String`: the part before the first `::` (the whole text when there is none), trimmed, every backslash replaced by a slash, a leading `./` removed, trailing slashes removed.
  3. `pub fn covers(pointer: &str, stored: &str) -> bool`: true when `path_of(pointer)` is not empty and equals `stored`, or `stored` starts with `path_of(pointer)` followed by `/` (the pointer names a folder and the file lies in it).
  4. `pub fn lies_in(pointer: &str, folder: &str) -> bool`: true when `path_of(pointer)` equals `folder`, or starts with `folder` followed by `/`.
  5. Unit tests: path_of(" src\\pump\\seal.rs::leak_model ") is `src/pump/seal.rs`; path_of("./src/pump/") is `src/pump`; covers("src/pump", "src/pump/seal.rs") is true; covers("src/pum", "src/pump/seal.rs") is false; covers("src/pump/seal.rs::f", "src/pump/seal.rs") is true; covers("", "a") is false; lies_in("src/pump/seal.rs", "src/pump") is true and lies_in("src/pump/seal.rs", "src/pum") is false; a path with spaces and one with non-ASCII letters work.
  6. Run cargo test --lib codeptr::
- accept: codeptr::path_of, covers and lies_in exist with their tests.
- verify: cargo test --lib codeptr::
- verified: 2026-11-25
- commit: 1de4fce
- reqs: R-CODE-6
- by: Reynan Henry Tandoyo

### T-474 · shown.rs: which entries a session has been shown already
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-474
- priority: P1 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-436
- why: A hook that repeats the same decisions at every edit of a file would be ignored after the third time.

- depends: T-468
- files: src/shown.rs, src/lib.rs
- read: docs/design.md, docs/format.md

  1. src/lib.rs: add `pub mod shown;` in alphabetical order.
  2. src/shown.rs: `pub fn unseen(state: &Path, session: &str, ids: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<String>>`. When `session` is empty or holds a character that is not an ASCII letter, a digit or `-`, return all of `ids` and write nothing. Otherwise the file is `<state>/shown/<session>.txt` with one ID per line: return the IDs of `ids` that are not in the file, in their order, and add them to the file (create the folder and the file when missing). An error of reading or writing is an Error with Code::Io that names the path.
  3. In the same call, remove every other file in `<state>/shown/` whose modified time is more than 30 days before the system time; an error while doing so is ignored.
  4. Unit tests in a temporary folder: the first call returns both IDs and the file holds them; the second call with one old and one new ID returns only the new one; another session name starts empty; a session name `a/b` returns everything and creates no file; a file given a modified time 31 days back (File::set_modified) is removed by the next call for another session.
  5. Run cargo test --lib shown::
- accept: shown::unseen returns the IDs a session has not been shown yet and records them.

### T-477 · guard: the entries that bind a file are shown before its first edit
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-477
- priority: P1 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-436
- why: This is the step that puts a decision in front of the LLM before it changes the code the decision is about (D51).
- summary: Before an LLM first changes a file in a session, its edit is refused once with the decisions, findings and lessons recorded for that file; it reads them and makes the edit again.
- depends: T-475, T-476, T-447
- files: src/cmd/guard.rs, tests/cmd_guard.rs
- read: docs/design.md, src/hooks.rs, src/cmd/after.rs, src/cmd/which.rs
- steps:
  1. src/cmd/guard.rs: add a private copy of the function `own` of src/cmd/after.rs (session_end.rs holds one too): the standard output of this program run again with the given arguments, None unless it ends with exit 0.
  2. src/cmd/guard.rs, `run`: when `hooks::guard` gives a message, fail with it as now. Otherwise, when `hooks::edited_path(&payload)` gives a path and `hooks::session_of(&payload)` gives a session, run `own(&["which", "--binding", <path>, "--session", <session>])`. Without a path or without a session, print nothing and succeed: without a session every edit would be refused again.
  3. When that output is not empty after trimming, fail with Code::Usage and the message: the line `Entries in force for <path>; read them, then make your edit again (dossier show <ID> prints one in full):`, a line break, then the output with its trailing line break removed. Exit code 2 makes Claude Code refuse this edit and hand the message to the LLM; its next edit of the file goes through, because which --session leaves out what this session was shown. When the output is empty or `own` gives None, print nothing and succeed: guard never fails for any other reason.
  4. tests/cmd_guard.rs: a project with an approved decision that has `code: src/pump`: an Edit payload for `src/pump/seal.rs` with `session_id` `s1` exits 2 and standard error holds the heading line and the decision's ID and title; the same payload again exits 0 with no output; the same payload with `session_id` `s2` exits 2 again; a payload without `session_id` exits 0 with no output; a payload for a file nothing points to exits 0 with no output; an Edit payload outside any dossier exits 0 with no output; the existing tests of edits inside DOSSIER pass unchanged.
  5. Update the module comment and the comment of `run`: guard now also shows, before the first edit of a file in a session, the entries in force that bind it. Run cargo test --test cmd_guard.
- accept: dossier guard refuses the first edit of a file in a session when entries in force bind it, names them, and lets the next edit through.
- verify: cargo test --test cmd_guard
- verified: 2026-11-25

- status: done

- steps:
  1. Create tests/retrieval.rs with the helpers of tests/common, as tests/cmd_search.rs uses them. One function builds the dossier: a person writes these approved entries, in this order, with the fixed clock one minute apart. Decisions (decide <text> --reason <reason>): D1 `Each rig command opens its own valve connection` / `Keeping a connection open needs a helper process.`; D2 `Pump seals are replaced every 500 hours` / `Two seals leaked after 600 hours.`; D3 `Speedline runs use the transient mode above 90 percent speed` / `Steady runs did not converge there.`; D4 `Results are stored as one file per run` / `One large file was lost twice.`; D5 `The bearing temperature limit is 95 degrees` / `The supplier names 100 degrees.`; D6 `The controller firmware is not updated during a campaign` / `An update changed the valve timing once.`; D7 `Every report names the rig and the date` / `Reports were mixed up.`. Findings (found <text>): F1 `Reusing one valve connection fails on the old controller`; F2 `Cavitation starts below 2 bar inlet pressure`; F3 `The rig log and the controller clock differ by two seconds`; F4 `The spare pump has a different impeller`. A glossary term: `term ControlLine --also 'valve connection' --meaning 'The line that opens the rig valve.'` (check the options with dossier help term).
  2. One table of questions: the words of a search and the title of the entry that must be among the first three results (full matches and those with some of the words taken together, in printed order): `connection reuse` → F1; `reused connections` → F1; `seal replacement` → D2; `storing results` → D4; `bearing temperature` → D5; `cavitation pressure` → F2; `firmware updates` → D6; `ControlLine` → D1; `impeller of the spare pumps` → F4; `transient speedline` → D3.

  5. A third test: `search xylophone marimba` prints `0 matches` and no line `some of the words:`.
  6. Run cargo test --test retrieval. If a question fails, do not change the question or the entries: give the task back with todo stuck and the failure message.

When the command asks for the person who said so, add `--said-by` with the owner's name from the answer. Never edit a file in DOSSIER directly.
  3. Delete topics-proposal.md (`git rm topics-proposal.md`).
  4. Run `dossier check`: it reports no dead code pointer. Run `dossier topics`: the line `(no topic)` shows 0, or name each entry left there in the done note.
  5. Run `dossier search connection reuse`: FND-011 and DEC-043 are among the first three results. If not, give the task back with the output.

### T-503 · 1.0.1: rare words are weighed against the whole dossier, and guard's refusal reads as a note
- status: done
- owner: planner
- priority: P1 · type: milestone
- goal: search's list of entries with some of the words and every section of brief --task weigh a word by how many entries of the whole dossier hold it, so a word that is common in the dossier never lifts an entry; brief --task lists at most 5 related entries; guard's refusal before an edit has no `error:` prefix. In the project's own dossier, search connection reuse lists FND-011 and DEC-043 among the first three results.
- why: A test of 1.0 on the project's own dossier (2026-11-25) found that select::ranked weighs words only within the pool it is given: brief --task listed the same unrelated dead end and investigation for every task, and search connection reuse put DEC-043 fourth.
- summary: Fixes from testing version 1.0 on the project's own dossier: related entries and partial search results are ranked against the whole dossier, brief --task lists fewer related entries, and the check before an edit no longer looks like an error.
- by: Reynan Henry Tandoyo
- note (2026-11-25, planner): added
- note (2026-11-25, planner): done — Ranking weighs words against the whole dossier (search, brief --task), brief --task lists at most 5 related, guard's refusal has no error: prefix, every dossier ignores .state/shown/, and an LLM adds an agreed topic with --said-by.

### T-526 · requirements.md and design.md: D54 and R-HAND, handover and takeover
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-526
- priority: P1 · difficulty: 1 · type: docs
- milestone: T-525
- why: Every task of this milestone names R-HAND-1 to R-HAND-5 and the outputs fixed in design.md section 22.
- summary: The requirements and the design say how a task is handed over and taken over.
- files: docs/requirements.md, docs/design.md
- read: docs/requirements.md, docs/design.md, src/todo_bridge.rs, src/taken.rs
- steps:
  1. docs/requirements.md, section 3: after the row of D53 add `| D54 | A task is handed over with ``handover <task> --note``, which gives it back in todo with a note of what is done and what is next, once the writer has returned every file taken for it. Anyone in the team takes over a task at any time with ``takeover <task>``; it is recorded who took over from whom, and the files the previous holder has not returned are named. An LLM may hand over its own task, and takes over only with ``--said-by <person>``. The handover note is a todo note on the task. (Owner, 2026-11-26.) | A colleague who changes team or falls ill must not leave a task locked or its progress lost. The task belongs to todo (D38), so the note is a todo note; a small team trusts each other, so a takeover is recorded rather than restricted. |` (doubled backticks stand for single ones). Line 3: `Draft 14, 2026-11-26 (owner's decisions: D28 to D54).`
  2. Directly before the heading `### 5.12 Remote mode — REMOTE` add the heading `### 5.11j Handover and takeover — HAND`, a blank line, the paragraph `A task is held in todo by the person or LLM that claimed it. These two commands move it to someone else without losing what was done (D54).`, a blank line and five items wrapped at 100 characters like the items of 5.11i:
  3. `- **R-HAND-1 MUST** ``handover <task> --note "<text>"`` is refused (Code::Refused) while the writer holds files taken for the task, naming each file and the commands ``dossier return <file> --done`` and ``--abandon``. Otherwise it adds to the task in todo the note ``handover — <text>``, gives the task back in todo (``todo release``), and writes a journal line with the event ``handover`` and the text as detail.`
  4. `- **R-HAND-2 MUST** ``takeover <task>`` claims the task in todo for the writer, with ``--force`` when someone else holds it, adds the note ``takeover — <writer> took over from <previous holder>`` (``from nobody`` when the task was open; `` (said by <person>)`` at its end when given), and writes a journal line with the event ``takeover``. For every file taken for the task by another person it prints ``<path>: taken by <person> on <time> and not returned; changes on their PC are not on the server``, then once ``take them with: dossier take <paths> --task <task> --force``. Last it prints what ``brief --task <task>`` prints. It never copies a file itself.`
  5. `- **R-HAND-3 MUST** An LLM runs ``takeover`` only with ``--said-by <person>``, resolved as ``decide`` resolves it; without it Code::NeedsPerson. ``handover`` needs no person.`
  6. `- **R-HAND-4 MUST** ``brief --task`` prints, directly after its first line, the last note of the task in todo that starts with ``handover —`` or ``takeover —``, as ``Last handover: <text after the dash> (<agent of the note>, <date of the note>)``.`
  7. `- **R-HAND-5 MUST** The name given to todo is the value of TODO_AGENT when it is set, otherwise the writer's name. When todo refuses or fails, the command fails with todo's message and writes no journal line.`
  8. docs/design.md: at the end add `## 22. Handover and takeover (R-HAND-1 to R-HAND-5, D54)` and a table `| Command | Arguments | Result |` with one row for `handover` (`<task> --note <text>`) and one for `takeover` (`<task> [--said-by <person>]`), whose Result cells repeat R-HAND-1 and R-HAND-2 with every output line exactly as written there, and the line `Both are writing commands (WRITING in src/ctx.rs) and run on the server in remote mode; takeover never copies files (R-FILE-4), it prints the take command for them.`
- accept: requirements.md defines D54 and R-HAND-1 to R-HAND-5, and design.md section 22 gives the two commands and their outputs.
- verify: git grep -q -F "**R-HAND-5 MUST**" -- docs/requirements.md && git grep -q -F "## 22. Handover and takeover" -- docs/design.md
- verified: 2026-11-26

### T-528 · handover: give a task back with a note, after its files are returned
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-528
- priority: P1 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-525
- why: A colleague who leaves a task must not leave it locked or lose what was done (R-HAND-1, R-HAND-5).
- summary: handover gives a task back in todo with a note of what is done and what is next, and refuses while the writer still holds files taken for it.
- depends: T-527
- files: src/cmd/handover.rs, tests/cmd_handover.rs
- read: docs/requirements.md, docs/design.md, src/todo_bridge.rs, src/taken.rs, src/journal.rs, src/cmd/take.rs, tests/cmd_brief.rs
- steps:
  1. src/cmd/handover.rs, `run`: load the context with `Ctx::load(g, "handover")` and the writer with `ctx.writer()`. Load the takes with `taken::load(&ctx.dossier, &ctx.cfg.code)` and `taken::all`; keep those whose `task` is the task (ignoring case) and whose `person` is the writer's person name. When there are any, fail with Code::Refused and the message: the line `<task>: return the files you took first:`, then one line per file `  <path> (taken <time>)`, then the line `dossier return <file> --done (or --abandon to drop your changes)`.
  2. The todo name is the value of the environment variable TODO_AGENT when it is set and not empty, otherwise the writer's name. Run `todo_bridge::json(&ctx.root, &["note", <task>, "handover — <text>", "--agent", <todo name>])`, then `todo_bridge::json(&ctx.root, &["release", <task>, "--agent", <todo name>])`. When either fails, return its error unchanged and write nothing else.
  3. Append one journal line (`journal::append(&ctx.state, ...)` as other commands build their Record) with the event `handover`, the task as id and the text as detail. Print `<task> handed over: handover — <text>`. JSON data: `{"task", "note"}`.
  4. tests/cmd_handover.rs (new, with tests/common as tests/cmd_brief.rs uses a todo stand-in): the stand-in todo records its arguments in a file and answers `{"ok":true,"data":{}}`: a handover calls todo note with `handover — Done: mesh; next: run 3` and then todo release for the task, and the journal has the line; with TODO_AGENT=anna-worker the todo calls pass `--agent anna-worker`; a writer who took a file for the task (dossier take, as tests/cmd_take.rs does) is refused with exit code of Code::Refused, the message names the file, and todo was not called; a stand-in todo that fails makes handover fail and writes no journal line.
  5. Run cargo test --test cmd_handover.
- accept: handover gives the task back in todo with its note and a journal line, and refuses while the writer holds files taken for the task.
- verify: cargo test --test cmd_handover
- verified: 2026-11-26

### T-529 · takeover: take over a task, name the unreturned files, show the progress
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-529
- priority: P1 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-525
- why: When a colleague is ill or gone, another must be able to carry on with everything recorded (R-HAND-2, R-HAND-3, R-HAND-5).
- summary: takeover claims a task for the writer, records who took over from whom, warns about files the previous holder has not returned, and shows the task's progress.
- depends: T-527
- files: src/cmd/takeover.rs, tests/cmd_takeover.rs
- read: docs/requirements.md, docs/design.md, src/todo_bridge.rs, src/taken.rs, src/journal.rs, src/cmd/decide.rs, src/cmd/after.rs
- steps:
  1. src/cmd/takeover.rs, `run`: load the context with `Ctx::load(g, "takeover")` and the writer. An LLM writer without --said-by fails with Code::NeedsPerson and `ask your person; with their yes: dossier takeover <task> --said-by <person>`. Resolve --said-by exactly as decide does.
  2. The todo name is TODO_AGENT when set and not empty, otherwise the writer's name. Read the task with `todo_bridge::json(&ctx.root, &["show", <task>])`; its `owner` (null or empty: nobody) is the previous holder. Claim with `["claim", <task>, "--agent", <todo name>]`, adding `"--force"` when the previous holder is someone else. Add the note `takeover — <writer> took over from <previous holder or nobody>`, with ` (said by <person>)` at its end when given. When a todo call fails, return its error unchanged and write nothing else. When the writer already holds the task, print `<task> is already yours` and change nothing.
  3. Append a journal line with the event `takeover`, the task as id and the note text as detail. Print `<task> taken over from <previous holder or nobody>`.
  4. From `taken::all`, for each take whose task is the task and whose person is not the writer, print `<path>: taken by <person> on <time> and not returned; changes on their PC are not on the server`; when there are any, print once `take them with: dossier take <paths separated by spaces> --task <task> --force`. Never copy or take a file.
  5. Last, run this program again with `brief --task <task>` (a private copy of `own` from src/cmd/after.rs) and append its output after a blank line. JSON data: `{"task", "from", "files": [{"path", "person", "time"}]}`.
  6. tests/cmd_takeover.rs (new, todo stand-in that records its arguments and answers show with an owner): a person takes over T-7 held by `ben`: claim with --force and the note `takeover — anna took over from ben` are sent, the journal has the line; an open task is claimed without --force and the note says `from nobody`; an LLM without --said-by is refused with Code::NeedsPerson and todo is not called; with `--said-by anna` the note ends with `(said by anna)`; a file ben took for T-7 is named with the warning line and the take command; a failing todo writes no journal line.
  7. Run cargo test --test cmd_takeover.
- accept: takeover claims the task for the writer with the recorded note, names the files others still hold with the command to take them, and shows the brief.
- verify: cargo test --test cmd_takeover
- verified: 2026-11-26

Change the existing expectations of the install data where they compare the whole data.
  6. Update the module comment of src/cmd/agents.rs. Run cargo test --lib agents::, cargo test --test cmd_agents and cargo test --test cmd_skill.

### T-565 · names.rs: the gate said_by_gate
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-565
- priority: P1 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-563
- why: Thirteen commands must decide in the same way whether an LLM may carry out a person's decision.
- summary: One function decides whether a command that needs a person's decision may run: for a person, or for an LLM that names its person.
- depends: T-564
- files: src/names.rs
- read: docs/design.md, docs/requirements.md, src/role.rs
- steps:
  1. src/names.rs: add `pub fn said_by_gate(who: &Who, said_by: Option<&str>, command: &str) -> Result<bool>` with the doc comment and exactly the five cases and messages of docs/design.md section 24, in that order. `said_by` is trimmed first, and an empty one counts as none. Names are compared in lower case. The role comes from `crate::role::current()`.
  2. So that the cases can be tested without the environment, put them in a private function `gate(who, said_by, command, role: crate::role::Role) -> Result<bool>` and let `said_by_gate` call it with `crate::role::current()`.
  3. Unit tests in src/names.rs for `gate`, with a person `anna` (name anna, person anna, is_llm false) and an LLM (name `anna - claude`, person anna, is_llm true): a person with no said_by is Ok(false); a person with `Anna` is Ok(false); a person with `ben` is Code::Usage; the LLM as a Worker is Code::Refused, also with `anna`; the LLM as a Planner with None, and with `  `, is Code::NeedsPerson with a message that holds `--said-by anna` and the command name; the LLM with `ben` is Code::NeedsPerson with a message that holds `acts for anna only`; the LLM with ` ANNA ` is Ok(true).
  4. Run cargo test --lib names::
- accept: names::said_by_gate exists with the five cases of design.md section 24 and their tests.
- verify: cargo test --lib names::
- verified: 2026-11-26
- commit: 7df744d
- reqs: R-SAID-1, R-SAID-4
- by: Reynan Henry Tandoyo
- note (2026-11-26, planner): added
- note (2026-11-26, haiku-T-565): done — Added names::said_by_gate, the one check that decides whether an LLM may carry out its person's decision with --said-by: a person runs as before, an LLM in a worker session is refused, an LLM without --said-by or for another person is refused, and an LLM with its person runs. Six unit tests in src/names.rs pass; the full suite, clippy and fmt pass.

### T-566 · approve: an LLM runs it with --said-by
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-566
- priority: P1 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-563
- why: The person's yes is given in the session; the LLM must be able to carry it out.
- summary: An LLM can run approve for its person after the person agreed, with both names on record.
- depends: T-565
- files: src/cmd/approve.rs, tests/cmd_approve.rs
- read: docs/design.md, docs/requirements.md, src/names.rs
- steps:
  1. src/cmd/approve.rs, Args (or the action's fields, for a subcommand): add `/// The person who decided this; needed when an LLM runs the command (D57)` `#[arg(long, value_name = "PERSON")] pub said_by: Option<String>`.
  2. src/cmd/approve.rs, `run`: replace the check `if who.is_llm { … Code::NeedsPerson … }` by `let said = names::said_by_gate(&who, args.said_by.as_deref(), "approve")?;` (add `use crate::names;` if it is missing), and refuse a run without a terminal (Code::NeedsTerminal) only when `said` is false.
  3. src/cmd/approve.rs: pass `said` to `review`. In `review`, when `said` is true: do not call `show`; after the check `rules::problems` (a draft that is missing something is still skipped with its warning), do not ask: call `approve(tx, item, &current, who)?` and record `Verdict::Approved`. The cases before the question (not a draft, an ID given twice) stay as they are. With `said` false nothing changes.
  4. Do not change what is written: `who` stays the name that runs the command, so the entry gets `by <who.person>` and the history line and the journal get `<person> via <llm>` as before for other commands. Update the module comment and the doc comment of `run`: an LLM runs it with --said-by (D57).
  5. tests/cmd_approve.rs: add four tests, with the helpers the file already uses (the project has the person `anna` with the LLM `anna-claude`, and the person `ben`). (a) `anna-claude` without --said-by: exit code 1, the message holds `--said-by anna`, and nothing changed. (b) `anna-claude` with `--said-by anna`, with no terminal and no answers prepared: it succeeds; the entry has `status: approved` and `approved: … by anna`, and the output is `<ID>: approved`; a second draft named in the same command is approved too; the newest history line of the entry holds `anna via anna-claude: approved`; the newest journal line has the person `anna`, the name `anna-claude` and `llm` true. (c) `anna-claude` with `--said-by ben`: exit code 1, the message holds `acts for anna only`, nothing changed. (d) as (b) but with `.env("DOSSIER_ROLE", "worker")` on the prepared command (`project.command(...)`): exit code 1, the message holds `a worker decides nothing`, nothing changed. The existing tests pass unchanged, except an existing test that expects the old message for an LLM: change it to expect `--said-by anna`.
  6. Run cargo test --test cmd_approve.
- accept: approve --said-by <its person> works for an LLM without a terminal; without it, with another name, or in a worker session it is refused.
- verify: cargo test --test cmd_approve
- verified: 2026-11-26
- commit: 0ad48dd
- reqs: R-SAID-1 to R-SAID-4, TEST-14
- by: Reynan Henry Tandoyo
- note (2026-11-26, planner): added
- note (2026-11-26, haiku-T-566): done — approve takes --said-by <person>: an LLM carries out its person's decision (D57), each draft that can be approved is approved without a question and the entry and journal name the person and the LLM; a person without a terminal is still refused, a worker session is refused. Four new tests in tests/cmd_approve.rs and the message test changed to --said-by; the approve tests (23), fmt, clippy and the full suite pass.

### T-613 · link: --as refines and --as contradicts
- status: done
- owner: worker-T-613
- priority: P2 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-604
- why: A plain link does not say that one entry narrows another or that two pull against each other (D61).
- summary: Two entries can be linked with a type: one refines the other, or the two contradict each other.
- depends: T-606
- files: src/cmd/link.rs, tests/cmd_link.rs
- read: docs/design.md, docs/format.md, docs/requirements.md
- steps:
  1. src/cmd/link.rs, Args: add `/// The type of the link: refines (the first entry narrows the second) or contradicts; without it a plain related link (R-WRITE-9)` `#[arg(long = "as", value_name = "TYPE")] pub as_type: Option<String>`.
  2. `run`, before the transaction: from the option, trimmed and in lower case, take three values: the field written into A, the field written into B, and the name of the type. None: `related`, `related`, `related`. `refines`: `refines`, `refined-by`, `refines`. `contradicts`: `contradicts`, `contradicts`, `contradicts`. Anything else: `Err(Error::new(Code::BadValue, "--as takes refines or contradicts"))`.
  3. `names` and `relate` take the field as a parameter instead of the constant RELATED. The detail of the history line and of the journal line is the field with `-` written as a space, then the other ID: `related FND-001`, `refines FND-001`, `refined by DEC-001`, `contradicts FND-001`. A names B when A's field for this type holds B; B names A when B's field for this type holds A.
  4. The text: without a type `<A> and <B>: linked` as now; with refines `<A> refines <B>`; with contradicts `<A> contradicts <B>`; `already linked` when both sides already hold the link of this type. The data gains `"as"` with the name of the type. Update the module comment and the doc comments (R-WRITE-9, D61).
  5. tests/cmd_link.rs: add tests. (a) `link DEC-001 FND-001 --as refines`: stdout is `DEC-001 refines FND-001\n`; DEC-001 has the line `- refines: FND-001` and one new history line ending in `changed — refines FND-001`; FND-001 has `- refined-by: DEC-001` and one new history line ending in `changed — refined by DEC-001`; taking the new lines away gives back the old text of each file, as the first test of the file checks for a plain link. (b) `--as contradicts`: both files get a `- contradicts:` line naming the other; stdout `DEC-001 contradicts FND-001\n`. (c) A second run of (a) prints `already linked` and adds no journal line. (d) `--as supersedes` fails with the exit code the file's test of a link to itself expects, and the message `--as takes refines or contradicts`; nothing is written. (e) A plain `link` after (b) still adds each entry to the other's related field. Tests use the helpers the test file already has (common::Project, the people anna and ben, the LLM anna-claude, the fixed clock) and invented text only.
  6. Run cargo test --test cmd_link.

  2. `struct Unsettled`: add `no_settle: usize` (open assumptions with no settle-by), `owed: usize` (approved lessons that owe a check) and `contradictions: Vec<(String, String)>`, each with a doc comment. `count_unsettled`: an open assumption without a settle-by adds one to `no_settle`; an approved entry of kind Lesson whose field `check`, trimmed, is not empty and whose field `check-state`, trimmed, is not `checked` adds one to `owed` (count it in its own `if` before the `match`, so a lesson can also count as changed by hand). ### T-620 · checked: a person says that a lesson's check catches its mistake
- status: done
- owner: worker-T-620
- priority: P2 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-604
- why: That a check is in place is a claim a person must stand for; once it is made, the lesson no longer counts as owing one (D62, D57).
- summary: A person, or an LLM with that person's yes, records that the test or hook named by a lesson really catches the mistake.
- depends: T-619, T-606
- files: src/cmd/checked.rs, tests/cmd_checked.rs
- read: docs/design.md, docs/requirements.md, src/cmd/reviewed.rs, tests/cmd_reviewed.rs, src/names.rs
- steps:
  1. src/cmd/checked.rs, `run`, built like `run` of src/cmd/reviewed.rs: `Ctx::load(g, "checked")`, the writer, `let said = names::said_by_gate(&who, args.said_by.as_deref(), "checked")?;`, and when `said` is false and `term::is_terminal()` is false, Code::NeedsTerminal with `this command must be run by a person at a terminal`. `--by`, trimmed, must not be empty: Code::BadValue, `say with --by how the check was shown to catch the mistake`.
  2. In one transaction (`tx::write`): get the entry with `store::get`. Refuse with Code::Refused when its kind is not Lesson (`<ID> is not a lesson`), when its status is neither Draft nor Approved (`<ID> is <status>; only a draft or approved lesson can be checked`), and when `--check`, trimmed, is empty and the field `check`, trimmed, is empty or missing (`<ID> names no check: give --check`).
  3. Then: set the field `check` when `--check` was given; set `check-state` to `checked`; add a history line with the event `checked` and the `--by` text as detail (`entry.add_history(&time, &who, "checked", by)`); when the lesson is approved and this is not a dry run, `approval::record(&tx.ctx().state, &id, text.as_bytes())?` as `reviewed` does; `tx.put` with `Change { id, event: "checked", detail: by }`. The text is `<ID>: checked`; the data is `{"id", "check", "by"}`. Write the module comment and the doc comments (R-WRITE-18, R-ENTRY-21, D62, D57).
  4. tests/cmd_checked.rs (new, built like tests/cmd_reviewed.rs). The four ways of TEST-14: anna-claude without --said-by is refused with exit code 1 and a message that holds `--said-by anna`, nothing changed; anna-claude with `--said-by anna`, with no terminal, succeeds: the lesson has `- check-state: checked`, its newest history line holds `anna via anna-claude: checked` and the --by text, and the newest journal line has the person anna, the name anna-claude and `llm` true; anna-claude with `--said-by ben` is refused (`acts for anna only`); the same with `.env("DOSSIER_ROLE", "worker")` on the prepared command is refused (`a worker decides nothing`). Also: `--check` sets the check field of a lesson that had none; a lesson with no check and no `--check` is refused; a decision is refused with `is not a lesson`; after `checked` on an approved lesson, `show` does not mark it `changed after approval`; an empty `--by` is refused.
  5. Run cargo test --test cmd_checked.
- accept: checked sets check-state: checked on a lesson for a person or for an LLM with --said-by, records who and how, refuses anything else, and leaves an approved lesson approved and unmarked.
- verify: cargo test --test cmd_checked
- verified: 2026-11-27

### T-621 · sweep: the pairs of entries in force that look alike, with the rules for judging them
- status: done
- owner: worker-T-621
- priority: P2 · difficulty: 1 · type: feature
- milestone: T-604
- why: Duplicates and contradictions were only caught at the moment of writing; nothing ever looked at the entries in force together (D63).
- summary: One command lists the entries that look alike so that a person can decide which one replaces, contradicts or refines the other. It changes nothing.
- depends: T-619
- files: src/cmd/sweep.rs, tests/cmd_sweep.rs
- read: docs/design.md, docs/requirements.md, src/select.rs, src/cmd/search.rs, src/store.rs
- steps:
  1. src/cmd/sweep.rs: the constant RULES exactly as docs/design.md section 25.6 gives it. `run`: `Ctx::load(g, "sweep")`, then `store::all(&ctx.dossier)` once; the store's warnings become warnings of the output. The candidates are the items with status Approved and kind Decision, Finding, Lesson or Howto, in a `Vec<Item>`.
  2. One `select::Index::of(&candidates)`. For each candidate build the query as `fn similar` of src/cmd/search.rs does: `tags` are the values of its fields `machine`, `analysis`, `software`, `tags` and `topic` (`entry.list(key)`), `words` are `select::words(&entry.title())`. `select::ranked_in(&candidates, &query, &index)` gives (score, item) pairs. Skip the candidate itself (same path). Skip a pair when either entry names the other, ignoring case, in one of the fields `related`, `refines`, `refined-by`, `contradicts`, `supersedes` or `superseded-by`.
  3. Keep each pair once, whichever side it was found from: the key is the two IDs in the order of the candidates, the value is the higher of the two scores (a BTreeMap or a Vec with a lookup is fine). Sort by score, highest first, then by the first ID, then by the second. Keep at most `args.limit` pairs.
  4. The text. No pair: `no entries in force look alike`. Otherwise: the first line `<n> pairs of entries in force look alike:` (for one: `1 pair of entries in force looks alike:`), an empty line, then per pair two lines `<ID> · <kind> · <title>` (kind as `Kind::name`) and an empty line, then RULES. The data: `{"pairs": [{"a": {"id", "kind", "title"}, "b": {…}, "score": <number>}…]}`. The command takes no lock and writes nothing: do not use `tx::write`. Write the module comment and the doc comments (R-SWEEP-1, R-SWEEP-2, D63, D7).
  5. tests/cmd_sweep.rs (new, built like tests/cmd_search.rs). (a) Two decisions by a person whose titles share their rare words, and one about something else: `sweep` prints `1 pair of entries in force looks alike:`, both IDs, and the line `- The same lesson under other conditions (Valid for) is not a duplicate.` of the rules; the third decision is not named. (b) After `link DEC-001 DEC-002` the output is `no entries in force look alike`. (c) A draft that looks like a decision (an LLM's lesson) is not paired. (d) With three look-alike entries, `--limit 1` prints one pair. (e) `--json` has `pairs` with the IDs, the kinds, the titles and a score. (f) The journal has as many lines after `sweep` as before, and every entry file is byte for byte the same. Tests use the helpers the test file already has (common::Project, the people anna and ben, the LLM anna-claude, the fixed clock) and invented text only.
  6. Run cargo test --test cmd_sweep.
- accept: sweep lists each pair of look-alike approved entries once, best first, leaves out linked pairs, prints the rules after them, and changes no file.
- verify: cargo test --test cmd_sweep
- verified: 2026-11-27
- commit: 3d68b90
- reqs: R-SWEEP-1, R-SWEEP-2, TEST-15
- by: Reynan Henry Tandoyo
- note (2026-11-27, planner): added
- note (2026-11-27, worker-T-621): done — sweep lists look-alike pairs with the rules

### T-413 · approve: the answer 'edit first'
- status: done
- owner: haiku-T-413
- priority: P1
- difficulty: 1
- type: feature
- milestone: T-058
- why: R-DRAFT-4 (MUST) names four answers; approve offered three, so a reader could not correct a draft before approving it (found in T-354).
- summary: During approve a person can open a draft in the editor, correct it, and then approve, reject or skip it.
- files: src/cmd/approve.rs, src/cmd/edit.rs, tests/cmd_approve.rs
- read: docs/requirements.md, src/cmd/edit.rs, tests/cmd_edit.rs
- steps:
  1. src/cmd/edit.rs: `fn editor_program`, `fn edit_in_temp_file` and `fn refuse_tool_lines` become `pub(crate) fn`; nothing else in edit.rs changes.
  2. src/cmd/approve.rs, review: keep `let mut current = item.entry.clone();` and ask in a loop with the prompt `<ID>: approve, edit first, reject or skip? (a/e/r/s) `. `e` or `edit`: run `crate::cmd::edit::edit_in_temp_file(&crate::cmd::edit::editor_program(), &id, &current.text())`; when the text came back unchanged, ask again; else parse it with Entry::parse, call `crate::cmd::edit::refuse_tool_lines(&current, &edited)` (an error ends the command, as in edit), add the history line `changed — edited before approval` with `edited.add_history(tx.time(), who, "changed", "edited before approval")`, set `current = edited`, show it again with show(&current.text()), check rules::problems(&current) as before the first question (problems: skipped with the same warning, but the edited text is still written), and ask again. `a`, `r` and anything else end the loop as now.
  3. src/cmd/approve.rs: approve and reject take the entry to write: `fn approve(tx: &mut Tx, item: &Item, entry: &Entry, who: &Who)` and `fn reject(tx: &mut Tx, item: &Item, entry: &Entry, who: &Who)` start from `entry.clone()` in place of `item.entry.clone()`. A skip after an edit queues the edited draft with `tx.put(item.path.clone(), Some(item), current.text(), change(id, "changed"))`, so that the edit is kept; a skip without an edit writes nothing, as now. Only one tx.put per draft. Update the module doc comment and the doc comment of review to name the four answers (R-DRAFT-4).
  4. tests/cmd_approve.rs: with the stand-in editor of tests/cmd_edit.rs that appends `Added by the editor.` (copy its two texts and write it with Project::write_stand_in), set as VISUAL: answers `e|a` approve the draft, its text contains `Added by the editor.`, its history has `edited before approval` before `approved`; answers `e|s` leave a draft that contains the added line; with an editor that saves the file unchanged, `e|r` rejects it without a `changed` history line.
  5. Run cargo test --test cmd_approve
- accept: approve asks a/e/r/s; e opens the editor, shows the changed draft and asks again; the edit is kept with a history line, whatever the answer after it.
- verify: cargo test --test cmd_approve
- verified: 2026-11-24
- commit: 1c0e914
- reqs: R-DRAFT-4
- by: Reynan Henry Tandoyo
- note (2026-11-23, planner): added
- note (2026-11-24, haiku-T-413): done
